records.text: An email authored by Jeffrey Epstein said 23andMe kits had arrived and would be delivered to Woody Allen and Soon-Yi Previn at their home.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But look at this email that Jeffrey Epstein authored to Woody (Woody Allen). It says the 23andMe kits arrived and will be delivered to Woody (Woody Allen) and Soon-Yi to their home today.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Reporting based on DOJ-released Epstein records reproduces a September 2016 message saying 23andMe kits had arrived and would be delivered to Woody Allen and Soon-Yi at their home. The existence and wording of the email are supported; no inference about why the kits were ordered is verified.

sources.title: Jeffrey Epstein Linked to DNA Test Kits for Prominent Figures in DOJ Records
sources.relevance: Reproduces the released email wording about kits for Woody Allen and Soon-Yi.

records.text: A second email said 30 23andMe kits were billed to James Miller and asked whether the shipping address was Jeffrey Epstein's home at 9 East 71st Street.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They're always blocking out the names, but it says, hi, Sultan (email addressee; full identity unverified), can you please tell me? Who James Miller is? He is who you have billed the 30 kids to. Also, do I understand the shipping address is Jeffrey (Jeffrey Epstein)'s home at 9 East 71st Street? We're talking about 23andMe kits.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. The released order-confirmation record shows James Miller as the billed customer for 30 kits and asks that they be shipped to 9 East 71st Street, matching the statement.

sources.title: EFTA02214255 — 23andMe Order Confirmation
sources.relevance: Released record lists James Miller, 30 kits, and 9 East 71st shipping address.

records.text: 23andMe was founded in 2005, shortly after the U.S. invasion of Iraq.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: well interestingly enough that that particular project 23andme or that particular business also began shortly following our invasion into Iraq. ... Well, in 2005, the now bankrupt company, 23andMe came together where people began sending in those DNA kits to figure out their ancestry.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. 23andMe official corporate materials and an SEC filing date the company to 2006, not 2005. Operation Iraqi Freedom began in March 2003, so the specific founding-year claim is false; shortly afterward is subjective.

sources.title: 23andMe Holding Co. SEC Form 10-K
sources.relevance: Official filing dates the predecessor company incorporation to 2006.

records.text: What was this mass campaign to effectively collect everybody on Earth's DNA by saying, 'We're going to help you with your ancestry'?
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So this brings me back to a 23andMe. If you follow that train of thought that they are actually doing things from a religious angle, a demonic angle, but they're presenting it as a science, what was this mass campaign to effectively collect everybody on Earth's DNA by saying, oh, look, we're going to help you with your ancestry.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. 23andMe does market ancestry services and has collected saliva/DNA samples from millions of registered customers. The literal everybody on Earth language and claimed hidden motive are hyperbole or unsupported, so only the factual collection-and-marketing core is verified.

sources.title: 23andMe Holding Co. SEC Form 10-K for 2025
sources.relevance: Reports millions of registered customers and DNA samples, supporting collection scale but not universal collection or motive.

sources.title: 23andMe DNA Test Kit Service Options
sources.relevance: Official product page confirms saliva DNA testing and ancestry service marketing.
